lines.en: What happens to the lanterns at the end of the festival?
lines.cn: 节庆结束时，那些灯笼会怎么样呢？

lines.en: A Festival for the Dead is held once a year in Japan.
lines.cn: 在日本，每年都会举行一次“亡灵节”（Festival for the Dead）。

lines.en: This festival is a cheerful occasion,
lines.cn: 这个节日是一个充满欢乐的场合。

lines.en: for on this day, the dead are said to return to their homes and they are welcomed by the living.
lines.cn: 因为据说在这一天，死者会回到他们的家中，而生者会迎接他们。

lines.en: As they are expected to be hungry after their long journey, food is laid out for them.
lines.cn: 由于他们在长途旅行后很可能会感到饥饿，所以已经为他们准备好了食物。

lines.en: Specially-made lanterns are hung outside each house to help the dead to find their way.
lines.cn: 每户人家的外面都挂有特制的灯笼，目的是帮助逝者在来世找到回家的路。

lines.en: All night long, people dance and sing.
lines.cn: 整晚，人们都在跳舞和唱歌。

lines.en: In the early morning the food that had been laid out for the dead
lines.cn: 清晨时分，那些原本为死者准备的食物……

lines.en: is thrown into a river or into the sea as it is considered unlucky for anyone living to eat it.
lines.cn: 这种动物会被扔进河流或海洋中，因为人们认为食用它的肉会给任何人带来厄运（即带来不幸）。

lines.en: In towns that are near the sea, the tiny lanterns which had been hung in the streets the night before,
lines.cn: 在那些靠近海边的小镇上，前一晚被挂在街上的那些小灯笼……

lines.en: are placed into the water when the festival is over.
lines.cn: 这些物品会在节日结束后被放入水中。

lines.en: Thousands of lanterns slowly drift out to sea guiding the dead on their return journey to the other world.
lines.cn: 成千上万的灯笼缓缓被放流入海，为逝者指引返回另一个世界的道路。

lines.en: This is a moving spectacle, for crowds of people
lines.cn: 这是一场令人感动的场面，成群的人们都聚集在一起观看。

lines.en: stand on the shore watching the lanterns drifting away until they can be seen no more.
lines.cn: 站在岸边，看着那些灯笼渐渐远去，直到它们完全消失在视线之外。
